subject: Helix Health: intermittent WebSocket chunk freeze impacting real-time triage
messages:
From: Martin O'Connor <martin.oconnor@helixhealth.com>
To: support@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Cc: suresh.p@helixhealth.com
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Realtime feed: sudden token stream freeze during high-volume triage

Hi team,

We started seeing repeated incidents this morning where the realtime websocket stream from Redwood suddenly stops emitting chunks for ~10-40s during high throughput (peak 1.2k RPS). Client-side shows an open socket but no token frames arrive — diagnostics show no TCP disconnect and no server 5xx in the immediate window. This is causing missed triage events in our live workflow.

I've attached logs and a pcap of a reproducer that happened at 08:51 PDT. Error rate spikes correlate with the freeze window and throughput increases. Please advise urgent next steps — this is affecting our on-call rotation and we have an executive Q at 1630.

Martin
Director, Platform Engineering
Helix Health

Attachments: helix_logs_20260824.tar.gz, ws_trace_08_24.pcap

From: priyom_das@redwood.ai
To: Martin O'Connor <martin.oconnor@helixhealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 09:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Realtime feed: sudden token stream freeze during high-volume triage

Hi Martin — thanks for the data (and the PCAP). Very sorry you're hitting this. We're treating as P0. Initial triage notes below:

- Observed symptom: streaming socket remains ESTABLISHED; token frames stop flowing for a burst window (~10-40s).
- Correlated signals: short-lived CPU pressure on a subset of serving pods, higher than usual concurrent KV cache invalidation activity, no consistent 5xx emitted from the gateway layer in customer logs.

Immediate plan:
1) I'll kick off a dedicated incident channel and escalate to SRE.
2) Can you confirm whether you were using the default batch/latency profile or had custom batching enabled? (this helps reproduce)
3) We'll ask for a short maintenance window tonight for a canary config change if we can't reproduce quickly.

Karthik — looping you in for the serving/runtime analysis (streaming transport + kernel selection).

I'll update within 45 minutes.

— Priyom
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: priyom_das@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Helix Health P0: streaming chunk freeze affecting production triage (exec awareness requested)

Marissa / Sean — I need executive attention on a P0 affecting Helix Health (key strategic healthcare customer, active annual committed plan). Summary: their realtime WebSocket streams intermittently stop producing token/chunk frames for 10-40s while sockets remain open. Error rate impact: customer telemetry shows 4.8% of requests during the window return partial responses; throughput degraded by ~18% for affected routes.

What we've done so far:
- Collected PCAP + logs from customer (attached).
- Initial triage points to transient CPU contention + aggressive KV cache invalidation during peak bursts on our Dedicated fleet routing for that account.
- Repro: single-run local repro attempted; could reproduce under artificial load when simulating concurrent cache flushes.

Risks / impact:
- Customer-facing triage misses in production; they have an executive Q this afternoon and have escalated to their CTO.
- Potential SLA/renewal risk if we don't provide a clear mitigation path in the next 12 hours.

Proposed immediate mitigations (short-term playbook):
1) Route Helix to a lower-latency dedicated pool (can reserve a warm pool) to avoid noisy neighbor CPU spikes.
2) Apply a temporary conservative KV cache invalidation window for their routes.
3) Increase socket-level keepalive and add a 3s heartbeat token at the app layer to detect silent stalls faster.
4) Provide Helix an exec-level timeline and a walk-through of proposed safe canary change.

Asks: please approve a) temporary capacity reservation and b) an SLA credit holdback contingency if remediation >24h. Also need ops support to prepare a canary build of the runtime with additional telemetry (server-side chunk timestamps) to ship by EOD.

I attached the logs and the PCAP. I'll open a JIRA (JIRA-7293) and a HubSpot ticket (HS-112233) and will coordinate the postmortem.

— Priyom

Attachments: helix_logs_20260824.tar.gz, ws_trace_08_24.pcap, error_sample_20260824.txt

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: priyom_das@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Cc: Martin O'Connor <martin.oconnor@helixhealth.com>, suresh.p@helixhealth.com
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Helix Health P0: streaming chunk freeze affecting production triage (exec awareness requested)

Thanks for the clear summary, Priyom. I've scheduled an exec sync at 17:30 PT today and will join the customer call. Sean — please prepare a one-slide impact summary and the proposed credit contingency. Karthik / SRE — prioritize the canary for the conservative KV invalidation and the heartbeat patch.

Immediate decisions:
- Approved: temporary capacity reservation (2 x warm GPU pods) for the Helix routes through midnight PT tomorrow. Ops: please enact ASAP and validate with a 15-minute smoke test.
- Approved: apply conservative cache invalidation policy for Helix only; revert if we observe downstream cost surge.

Customer comms: Priyom, take point on the 16:30 CTO update. Offer the customer the option for a rolling canary tonight and a detailed postmortem within 72 hours.

Follow-ups assigned:
- Karthik: runtime telemetry patch and quick repro notes (JIRA-7293) — due EOD.
- Ops: capacity reservation + smoke test — 60 min.
- Priyom: customer update and exec call — ongoing.

Thanks all — Marissa
VP, Customer Success | Redwood Inference
